## Design

### 2026-10-04 — Project planning & component research.

**1h**

Project planning & component research.

I started planning out Reflex to figure out what the project needs. I decided that the most basic system will use a push button, an LED, and a microcontroller. Below is the basic system layout.

![Screenshot 2026-10-04 094820](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cavLLmYzVkZWo0utyyD4hUaCvcnGNniC/aeb3c175a1deb2b0ef86a52b1693f1377bfe9348708d505fbc999faa9c180a3b.png)

The LED will turn on after a random delay. After it turns on, it will start counting the time taken until the button is pressed.

After I looked a little deeper into what hardware I wanted, I made a ReadME.

![Screenshot 2026-10-04 100347](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cavLLmYzVkZWo0utyyD4hUaCvcnGNniC/de96baea9180bdc280ffcc48f44f04964a484f0a6cd937e29185d14532c1be1b.png)

### 2026-10-04 — Adding parts to the Bill of Materials

**0.5h**

Adding parts to the Bill of Materials

While I was looking for the specific listings of parts, I realized that inflation hit pretty hard and I can't get everything under $30. I reduced my costs as much as possible by looking for a kit and removing the OLED display from the design.

### 2026-10-04 — Starting Firmware and cooking up the PCB.

**5h**

Starting Firmware and cooking up the PCB.

Firmware:
Using the Pin library, I'm able to easily code with the ports on the Raspberry Pi in python. After I set up the components with the ports, I made the logic for turning on the LED and counting the time to receive the button input. The random library is used to create a random starting time, and some while loops and if statements are used to prevent cheating by pressing the button before it starts.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cavLLmYzVkZWo0utyyD4hUaCvcnGNniC/ecc9ec7ac5f4aafbe8b8dd70417902461aa9039b6fbd510fcd4f71f2cf3651ea.png)

PCB:
Since I have briefly used KiCAD before, I decided to start using KiCAD (as opposed to other softwares) and made a schematics layout for my design. I simply had to include the few parts that I need and
![Screenshot 2026-10-04 140023](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cavLLmYzVkZWo0utyyD4hUaCvcnGNniC/37e061e274b61e343c0bd3ed41133169fd59fbe156c8cca2bf79ba06c1564414.png)

Afterwards, I had to attach footprints to the different pieces that I added in order to make sure that the part assignments correctly correspond to the parts that I have requested.
![Screenshot 2026-10-04 124207](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cavLLmYzVkZWo0utyyD4hUaCvcnGNniC/07bab89c8fda2c4e750f8f5f2f8f773931ebd48ef3197b8268c66cf6cec1eec6.png)

I then used the KiCAD tools to update PCB from a schematic, creating this:
![Screenshot 2026-10-04 124905](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cavLLmYzVkZWo0utyyD4hUaCvcnGNniC/9ba03208c6e5c205705c4402124d733fd637fed748c071ad3607b402b4a3b0e0.png)

I then had to move pieces around for organization, and then I connected the ports together. (Ground to ground, Out to out, in to in). Then, I realized that I needed to have other unused ports grounded, which I did by creating a giant red sheet of copper. After packing everything as tightly as possible, I also surrounded it with the board outline.
![Screenshot 2026-10-04 132144](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cavLLmYzVkZWo0utyyD4hUaCvcnGNniC/840ade23a07e746a6a8ce3a01eabe3ad2fc07fbe82de0b10272c4c44e4958596.png)

With that PCB model complete, I was able to view the 3D preview in KiCAD, shown below.
![Screenshot 2026-10-04 132621](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cavLLmYzVkZWo0utyyD4hUaCvcnGNniC/7368ca47cd5c1f7e40f8bf76502071376c395d681dd0764b09ab87c215e1c3cb.png)
